newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-SPAIN KNOCKED OUT AFTER SECOND SANCHEZ DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN KNOCKED OUT AFTER SECOND SANCHEZ DEFEAT.

text.p: Belgium knocked out favourites Spain in the first round of the Fed Cup world group as Arantxa Sanchez Vicario suffered her second defeat in two days to give the Belgians an unbeatable 3-0 lead.
The former world number one, already beaten by substitute Els Callens on Saturday, was beaten 6-3 2-6 8-6 by Belgium's leading player Sabine Appelmans.
Belgium will face France in the semifinals.

Sanchez Vicario, who had won her six previous matches against world number 19 Appelmans, saved a first match point in the ninth game but the Belgian sealed victory in the 14th game on Sanchez Vicario's serve.
Spain have won the Cup four times in the past six years, including victories over the United States in 1991, 1994 and 1995.
World number four Sanchez Vicario was under pressure from the start.
She saved three set points in the ninth game of the first set but went down to the fourth when Appelmans hammered a double-fisted backhand down the line.
Appelmans tired in the second set but recovered her poise just in time, saving two break points in the first game of the final set.
She broke Sanchez in the sixth game and carved out a 5-2 lead. Sanchez Vicario broke back for 5-4 but finally went down amid thunderous applause from the partisan crowd.
"After the second set I thought I would't make it. I was getting tired but then I found myself leading again...I'm exhausted," Appelmans said.
Spain were without Conchita Martinez, who formed with Sanchez Vicario the most successful doubles combination in Cup history. Martinez has tendinitis in her right shoulder.

Belgium were also weakened by the absence of Dominique Van Roost, who had not fully recovered from an abdomen injury which had forced her to retire in the quarter-finals of the Australian Open. Van Roost had knocked out Sanchez Vicario in the third round of the Australian Open.
